CORRECTED_model.physiological_latent_state: z_phys(t) = [v(t), c(t)] — venous congestion burden + cranial compliance
CORRECTED_model.prediction: r(t+H) = P(y(t+H)=1 | z_phys(1:t), θ) — failure risk is a PREDICTION from the physiological state, NOT a component of the state itself
CORRECTED_model.why_this_matters: Failure risk is NOT a physiological state. It is a prediction ABOUT the physiological state. Putting it inside z(t) is a category error. The physiological state drives the prediction; the prediction does not drive the state.
CORRECTED_model.observations: X(t) = [x1(mean ICP), x2(ICP pulse amplitude), x3(CVP), x4(sigmoid pressure), x5(anterior SSS pressure)]
CORRECTED_model.state_equation: z_phys(t+dt) = f(z_phys(t), u(t), θ) + w(t)  [process noise]
CORRECTED_model.prediction_model: r(t+H) = g(z_phys(1:t), θ)  [trained on outcome data]

state_split.what_changed_from_Round_51: r(t) removed from z_phys(t). Failure risk is now a PREDICTION from the physiological state trajectory, not a state component.

observability_analysis.label: MODEL-BASED OBSERVABILITY HYPOTHESIS — not clinical evidence
what_is_defined: f(): state evolution — z_phys(t+dt) depends on current venous congestion, compliance, treatment input, and patient-specific parameters. Specific functional form NOT yet defined.
h(): observation model — X(t) depends on z_phys(t) through physiological relationships (e.g., CVP reflects venous congestion, ICP pulse reflects compliance). Specific functional form NOT yet defined.
θ: patient-specific parameters (venous resistance, CSF compliance, absorption capacity). NOT yet estimated.
what_is_NOT_defined: The exact functional form of f() and h() — these require physiological modeling
The parameter vector θ — these require patient-specific estimation
The noise structure (process noise w, measurement noise v) — these require empirical characterization
observability_tests_needed: LOCAL OBSERVABILITY: linearize h() around an operating point and check the observability Gramian rank. If rank < dim(z_phys), the state is not locally observable from the measurements.
PARAMETER IDENTIFIABILITY: can θ be uniquely determined from X(t) data? Or are there parameter degeneracies?
NOISE SENSITIVITY: how much measurement noise can the system tolerate before the state estimate becomes unreliable?
SENSOR DROPOUT: if x3-x5 (venous signals) are unavailable (currently episodic), can the state still be estimated from x1-x2 alone? (Round 51 Case 4 suggests NO — but this needs formal proof)
CONFOUNDING: can other physiological variables (e.g., cardiac output, blood pressure, PaCO2) produce the same X(t) changes as z_phys(t) changes?
observability_analysis.honest_status:
The synthetic separability tests in Round 51 demonstrated that DIFFERENT assumed states CAN produce different observations under an ASSUMED h(). But this is NOT a formal identifiability proof because h() is not specified. The tests show the CONCEPT is plausible, not that it WORKS.

CORRECTED LABEL: IDENTIFIABILITY HYPOTHESIS — synthetic separability demonstrated under assumed h(). NOT proven.
what_would_constitute_proof: 1. Define f() and h() from physiological first principles (fluid mechanics, compliance models)
2. Compute the observability Gramian and verify rank = dim(z_phys)
3. Test with simulated data (known z_phys → X → recover z_phys)
4. Test with clinical data (measured X → estimated z_phys → compare with clinical outcomes)

competing_models.name: Venous congestion + compliance model
competing_models.latent_state: z_phys = [v(t) venous congestion, c(t) cranial compliance]
competing_models.hypothesis: Persistent headache after VSS is caused by residual venous congestion (elevated CVP, abnormal sinus distribution) and/or abnormal cranial compliance that is not reflected in mean ICP.
supporting_evidence: 2026 study: elevated CVP, higher anterior SSS pressure, BMI associated with worse outcomes (OBSERVED ASSOCIATION)
2026 study: proposed increased dural compliance as mechanism (HYPOTHESIS)
The R2-C3 anomaly (headache despite normal ICP) is consistent with a non-ICP physiological cause
weaknesses: Association ≠ causation (CVP may be a marker, not the cause)
Compliance inference from ICP pulse amplitude is NOT established as a unique mapping
Assumes the anomaly has a SINGLE physiological explanation (venous/compliance)
Circularity risk: chose v and c, then chose observations expected to identify them
competing_models.circularity_risk: HIGH — the state was chosen BEFORE the observations were chosen. Need to test if data-driven state discovery produces the same structure.

competing_models.name: Migraine/CGRP-dominant model
competing_models.hypothesis: Persistent headache after VSS is caused by coexisting migraine biology (CGRP-mediated) that was present before VSS and persists after VSS, independent of venous/CSF physiology.
supporting_evidence: 2024 prospective study: higher serum CGRP in IIH patients with persistent headache after ICP normalization (OBSERVED)
2026 experimental work: CGRP can induce headache attacks in IIH patients (OBSERVED)
Repeat-stenting series: authors explicitly state chronic migraine can coexist after pressure normalization (CLINICAL JUDGMENT)
72.2% persistent headache in repeat-stenting series while only minority required surgery (OBSERVED)
weaknesses: Does not explain WHY some patients with normal CVP and normal CGRP still have headache
CGRP is not routinely measured in IIH patients
Migraine and IIH headache may OVERLAP, not be separate — making a binary distinction impossible
competing_models.circularity_risk: LOW — the model is derived from clinical observations (CGRP data), not from a pre-chosen state definition.

competing_models.name: Mixture model (venous + migraine)
competing_models.latent_state: z_phys = [v(t) venous congestion, m(t) migraine/CGRP state, c(t) compliance]
competing_models.hypothesis: Persistent headache after VSS has MULTIPLE causes that coexist in the same patient. Some patients have venous congestion, some have migraine biology, some have BOTH. The latent state is a MIXTURE, not a single explanation.
supporting_evidence: Both Model A and Model B have supporting evidence
Clinical reality is that IIH and migraine are COMORBID, not mutually exclusive
The 57% recurrence may contain MULTIPLE subgroups (as the CEO noted in Round 46)
CGRP can induce headache in IIH patients — suggesting the systems interact, not just coexist
weaknesses: More complex — requires more parameters and more data to identify
May be unidentifiable if the mixture components are confounded
Requires measuring BOTH venous signals AND CGRP/migraine markers — more invasive
competing_models.circularity_risk: MODERATE — derived from combining two evidence-backed models, but the mixture weights are unknown.

competing_models.name: Measurement artifact / endpoint misclassification
competing_models.latent_state: z_phys = [NONE — the 'recurrence' is not a real physiological state]
competing_models.hypothesis: The 57% 'recurrence' is partly a MEASUREMENT/ENDPOINT problem. 'Headache recurrence' is subjective and may not reflect IIH pathology at all. The patients may have medication-overuse headache, tension-type headache, or other non-IIH conditions that were never properly diagnosed.
supporting_evidence: The repeat-stenting series found 72.2% headache but only 17% needed surgery (OBSERVED) — suggesting most 'recurrence' is NOT objective IIH failure
The 178-patient study found recurrence despite ICP/papilledema improvement (OBSERVED) — suggesting the endpoint may be measuring something other than IIH
weaknesses: Does not explain the SUBSET of patients who DO have objective findings (new stenosis, elevated ICP) — those are real failures
Even if some recurrence is misclassified, the VENOUS associations (CVP, SSS pressure) suggest a physiological component
competing_models.circularity_risk: LOW — this model challenges the existence of the problem itself, which is the strongest anti-circularity position.

competing_models.name: Data-discovered latent structure
competing_models.latent_state: z_phys = [UNKNOWN — to be discovered from data]
competing_models.hypothesis: The latent state structure should be DISCOVERED from clinical data (e.g., unsupervised clustering, factor analysis, latent variable models) rather than hypothesized in advance.
supporting_evidence: The CEO's directive: 'What latent state best explains the observations?' not 'Can our chosen latent state be recovered?'
Model A has circularity risk (chose state then chose observations)
Multiple competing models (A-D) suggest the true structure is unknown
weaknesses: Requires a dataset that does NOT currently exist (multi-signal measurements + outcomes in IIH patients)
Unsupervised methods can find spurious structure in small datasets
May discover structure that is not physiologically interpretable
competing_models.circularity_risk: NONE — the state structure is determined by data, not by the modeler.

model_comparison.ranking_criteria: Evidence strength × non-circularity × clinical plausibility × testability

ranking.rationale: STRONGEST — both venous AND migraine evidence are source-backed. The mixture model does not assume a single explanation. It acknowledges that the 57% may contain multiple subgroups. It is the most HONEST model because it does not pre-select one cause.
ranking.weakness: Most complex. Requires the most data. But complexity is warranted by the heterogeneity of the evidence.

ranking.rationale: STRONGEST anti-circularity position. Challenges the problem's existence. The 2026 review says outcome definitions are unresolved, and 72.2% headache with only 17% needing surgery supports this. Must be ruled OUT before any physiological model is accepted.
ranking.weakness: Does not explain the subset with objective findings. But it correctly challenges the majority.

ranking.rationale: STRONG evidence (2024 CGRP study, 2026 CGRP induction). Low circularity. Derived from clinical observations. But does not explain all cases.
ranking.weakness: Does not address the venous associations found in the 2026 study.

ranking.rationale: MODERATE evidence (2026 associations). But HIGH circularity risk — chose state then chose observations. Compliance inference not established. Must compete against B and C, not be assumed.
ranking.weakness: Circularity risk is the biggest problem. The model may be an artifact of how it was constructed.

ranking.rationale: NO circularity. But NO data exists to discover from. This is the IDEAL approach but is not yet actionable.
ranking.weakness: Requires a prospective dataset that does not exist.

model_comparison.the_key_insight:
The CEO is right: the breakthrough may not be a single 'venous congestion' state. It may be a MIXTURE / PHENOTYPE IDENTIFICATION problem.

The 57% recurrence likely contains:
  - Some patients with venous congestion (Model A)
  - Some patients with migraine/CGRP biology (Model B)
  - Some patients with BOTH (Model C)
  - Some patients with misclassified endpoints (Model D)

The invention opportunity is NOT 'build a venous congestion sensor.'
It is: 'build a system that DISTINGUISHES between these phenotypes and selects the appropriate intervention for each.'

This is a PHENOTYPE IDENTIFICATION + INTERVENTION SELECTION capability, not a single-variable measurement.

redefined_technical_effect.OLD_definition: DISTINGUISHING IIH-related headache (venous) from non-IIH headache (migraine) — REMOVED (too strong, assumes binary separation that CGRP data contradicts)
redefined_technical_effect.NEW_definition: IDENTIFYING A PHYSIOLOGIC TREATMENT-FAILURE PHENOTYPE among patients whose conventional ICP endpoints have normalized — without assuming the underlying biology prematurely
why_this_is_stronger: Does NOT assume the cause is venous (could be migraine, mixture, or artifact)
Does NOT assume a binary separation (IIH vs migraine — the CGRP data shows overlap)
DOES define the target: a phenotype (treatment failure) among a specific population (normalized ICP)
DOES leave the biology open: the latent structure is to be DISCOVERED, not pre-assumed
redefined_technical_effect.the_research_question: Among VSS-treated IIH patients with normalized ICP and improved papilledema, can multi-modal physiological measurements (venous pressures, ICP waveform, CGRP, clinical phenotype) identify a latent structure that predicts which patients will have persistent headache — and does that structure contain multiple distinguishable phenotypes (venous, migraine, mixed, artifact)?
redefined_technical_effect.what_this_changes:
The invention is NOT a venous congestion sensor.
The invention is NOT a migraine diagnostic.
The invention is a PHENOTYPE IDENTIFICATION SYSTEM that uses multi-modal physiology to classify treatment-failure patients into actionable subgroups (venous intervention, migraine treatment, combined, or reclassification) — a capability that no current system has.

what_changed: State split corrected: z_phys = [v, c], r(t+H) = prediction (not state component)
Identifiability downgraded: PROVEN → MODEL-BASED HYPOTHESIS (h() unspecified)
Competing models introduced: 5 models, Model C (mixture) ranked strongest
Circularity risk acknowledged: Model A (venous+compliance) has HIGH circularity
Technical effect redefined: NOT 'distinguish IIH from migraine' but 'identify treatment-failure phenotype among normalized-ICP patients'
CGRP evidence incorporated: 2024 serum CGRP study + 2026 CGRP induction weaken the binary venous/migraine distinction
verdict.the_honest_state:
The machine does NOT know what latent structure explains the R2-C3 anomaly. It has 5 competing models. Model C (mixture) is the most honest because it does not pre-select one cause. The true structure must be DISCOVERED from data, not assumed.

The invention opportunity is NOT a specific sensor or valve. It is a PHENOTYPE IDENTIFICATION SYSTEM that uses multi-modal physiology to classify treatment-failure patients into actionable subgroups.
what_must_happen_before_mechanism: 1. COLLECT DATA: prospective multi-signal measurement (venous + ICP waveform + CGRP + clinical) in VSS patients with outcomes
2. DISCOVER STRUCTURE: apply unsupervised/semi-supervised methods to identify the latent phenotype structure
3. VALIDATE PREDICTION: does the discovered structure predict R2-C3 recurrence out-of-sample?
4. TEST INTERVENTION: does phenotype-guided intervention selection improve outcomes?
5. PATENTABILITY: is the phenotype identification + intervention selection system novel at the claim level?
verdict.gate_status: YELLOW — the problem is real, the anomaly is real, the competing models are defined, and the technical effect is honestly scoped. But the latent structure is UNKNOWN and must be discovered from data.
verdict.mechanism_status: UNPROPOSED — the machine must first discover the latent structure from data before it can generate mechanisms. The mechanism depends on WHICH phenotype(s) exist and WHICH interventions address them.
